Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear list.

Quick answers up front:
- Trial conversion: we support both meter-based conversion (post-trial metered usage starts) and a single activation event (one-off entitlement activation) depending on how you want to represent it. We typically recommend meter-based for usage-driven products and activation-charge for seat-based seat-upsells.
- Billing cadence: AWS issues a monthly invoice for Marketplace SaaS charges; Redwood settles to your seller account on a 30-45 day payout cadence by default. We can request an accelerated settlement for go-lives (requires Marketplace seller ops approval).
- Mapping file: I’m attaching our entitlement mapping template (DF_SaaS_Entitlement_Mapping.xlsx) and a short invoice sample for reference.

Looping in Ben Carter (billing ops) and Marissa Cole (marketplace integrations) to confirm the webhook payload we recommend for consumption and the exact field names in the mapping. Ben/Marissa — can you confirm the recommended webhook cadence (immediate events vs. batched hourly) and whether we should include an activation sentinel for trials?

Next step: Ben, can you draft the recommended webhook contract snippet and an example of the invoice line items we expect to see from AWS that should reconcile to DataFoundry's ledger?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Integrations | Redwood Inference

Thanks Kim — adding the details below.

Proposal (summary):
1) Trial conversion handling
   - Option A (recommended for DF): meter-based. Trial period flags start usage to 0; on conversion we mark the first billable meter event with "activation=true" and include a metadata tag (customer_id, sku_id, trial_id). This avoids separate one-off charges and maps cleanly to usage rows in AWS invoices.
   - Option B: activation charge — useful if you need a distinct onboarding fee.

2) Webhook / reconciliation cadence
   - Delivery: POST to your /marketplace/webhook endpoint
   - Payload: array of events (we recommend batched hourly for stability) OR single-event immediate for low-latency reconciliation.
   - Fields we include: timestamp, aws_sku, internal_sku, quantity, price_per_unit, event_type (usage|activation|refund), invoice_id (if assigned), marketplace_region.

3) Invoice line mapping (what we expect from AWS invoice vs. your ledger)
   - AWS invoice line: aws_sku, description, quantity, net_amount, tax, invoice_period
   - Your ledger: internal_sku, customer_id, recognized_revenue_period, settlement_status

Attachments: invoice_samples.pdf (examples of AWS invoice lines and how we tag them), webhook_contract_snippet.txt (minimal sample payload + endpoint requirements).

Next steps / asks:
- Sanjay: confirm you’re comfortable with batched hourly events vs. immediate delivery (we can do either).
- Procurement: we’ll need your preferred remittance details so we can map payout -> seller ledger.
- Kim/Marissa: I’ll load a baseline mapping into the HubSpot record and share a Google Sheet link for collaborative edits.

Onboarding can be done in two waves: canary tenant (1 week) -> full listing. For payout terms faster than 30 days we’ll need marketplace ops sign-off; let me know if you want me to escalate.

Cheers,
Ben Carter

- For settlement cadence, can you confirm whether Redwood can request an accelerated payout (15-day) for our account for the first 90 days post-launch? If yes, what additional paperwork is required?

Also: can we do a one-week canary starting Oct 20 (10/20 -> 10/27) for 20 customers, then open to full listing the following week? That scheduling works for our internal ops.
